rich_summary: After the demon Trishiras wounds Rama, the prince responds with overwhelming precision: he destroys the demon’s chariot, slays his horses and charioteer, and finally severs his three heads. The surviving rakshasas flee, but their leader Khara—enraged by the destruction of his army and generals—charges into battle. What follows is a vast, storm-like duel. Rama and Khara fill the sky with arrows until the sun itself seems darkened. Khara briefly gains advantage by shattering Rama’s bow and armor, but Rama calmly takes up the divine Vaishnava bow given by the sage Agastya. With dazzling archery he destroys Khara’s banner, chariot, horses, and weapons. As the demon stands on foot with a mace, the gods and sages gather in the sky to witness the heroic confrontation, recognizing Rama’s extraordinary might and righteousness.

highlight_spans.why: The opening moment where Trishiras wounds Rama, provoking the devastating retaliation that begins the battle sequence.
Rama’s decisive killing of Trishiras, including the striking image of the demon’s three heads being severed.
The immense scale of the duel as Rama and Khara fill the sky with arrows and darken the sun.
Rama takes up the divine Vaishnava bow given by Agastya, emphasizing his sacred backing and heroic destiny.
The turning point where Rama systematically destroys Khara’s chariot, weapons, and defenses.
The gods and sages assemble in the sky to praise Rama, marking the battle as a cosmic event witnessed by divine beings.

top_scenes.scene_text: Rama releases a storm of arrows that slice off the three heads of the demon Trishiras while his body still stands amid the battlefield.
Rama and Khara stand amid a sky darkened by countless arrows, their volleys crossing like fiery streaks that blot out the sun.
Rama, holding the radiant Vaishnava bow, shatters Khara’s chariot while gods and sages gather in the heavens watching the battle below.
